security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, the instruction trace interface (TraceCoreInterface) signals (itype, iaddr, ilastsize, priv) are only updated and valid when a new instruction block retires (iretire non-zero). If data trace were implemented with dretire for multi-memory-access instructions (vector load/store, Zcmp cm.push/cm.pop), the instruction context signals would be stale or invalid during cycles where dretire is asserted without iretire, because XiangShan currently ties all instruction context validity to iretire > 0 in the ROB commit path (Rob.scala:1284: traceValids(i) := io.commits.isCommit && io.commits.commitValid(i)). There is no mechanism to hold/latch instruction trace context across cycles when only data sub-accesses retire without corresponding instruction retirement.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: dretire asserted without corresponding iretire context validity; multi-memory-access instruction trace context not preserved/stalled during split data retirement; trace instruction context signals (itype/iaddr/ilastsize) not qualified by dretire-only validity window
security_spec.summary: When dretire fires without iretire for multi-access vec/Zcmp instructions, instruction-trace context signals must remain valid; current ROB commit-to-trace path in XiangShan invalidates context on iretire boundaries only, causing trace decoder to misattribute data accesses to wrong instructions

findings.finding: TracePipe defines only itype, iretire, and ilastsize — there is NO dretire (data retirement) field. The entire XiangShan trace subsystem is a one-dimensional instruction-retirement-only architecture. The vulnerability condition (dretire asserted without iretire context) cannot manifest because dretire does not exist as a concept anywhere in this RTL. For vector load/store or Zcmp cm.push/cm.pop instructions, each instruction commits once through the ROB and emits a single iretire entry with an instruction-retirement count — there is no per-element or per-access data-retirement tracking.

The TraceCoreInterface output to the external encoder carries per-group {iaddr, itype, iretire, ilastsize} but has NO dretire or dtype field. This is the core-to-encoder boundary. If an external trace encoder (e.g., XSTOP) were to interpret iretire as an E-Trace format-level 'Instruction Retirement' packet, it would have no visibility into whether constituent data accesses have completed. However, since Zcmp is not decoded in the trace path and vector ld/st produce itype=None entries, the interface is internally consistent for its current one-dimensional use case.

The ROB commit stage correctly drives traceCommitInfo signals (itype, iretire, ilastsize, ftqIdx, ftqOffset) for each commit slot. traceValids(i) is gated on io.commits.isCommit && io.commits.commitValid(i), which is the instruction-commit validity window. There is NO stale or invalid state because XiangShan does not implement dretire-only retirement cycles. The ROB state machine has only s_idle and s_walk states — no mechanism for data-only retirement cycles. Exception handling (lines 1287-1294) correctly forces itype to Exception/Interrupt, iretire to 0, and validity to true. This logic is internally self-consistent.
findings.snippet:
traceBlockInPipe(i).itype := rawInfo(i).traceBlockInPipe.itype
traceBlockInPipe(i).iretire := iretireCommit(i)
traceBlockInPipe(i).ilastsize := rawInfo(i).traceBlockInPipe.ilastsize
traceValids(i) := io.commits.isCommit && io.commits.commitValid(i)
when(io.exception.valid){ // trace exception
  traceBlocks(i).bits.tracePipe.itype := Mux(io.exception.bits.isInterrupt,
    Itype.Interrupt, Itype.Exception)
  traceValids(i) := true.B
  traceBlockInPipe(i).iretire := 0.U
}

findings.finding: io.commits.isCommit is defined as state === s_idle && !blockCommit. The ROB state machine has exactly two states: s_idle (normal operation) and s_walk (TLB walk). There is no s_dretire state or any mechanism for data-only retirement cycles, because data-retirement as a separate concept does not exist in XiangShan. The blockCommit signal incorporates traceBlock backpressure from the TraceBuffer. All commit-validity signaling is tied to instruction retirement — there is no split between instruction-side and data-side retirement.
findings.snippet:
val traceBlock = io.trace.blockCommit
val blockCommit = misPredBlock || lastCycleFlush || hasWFI || io.redirect.valid ||
  (deqNeedFlush && !deqHasFlushed) || deqFlushBlock || criticalErrorState || traceBlock
io.commits.isWalk := state === s_walk
io.commits.isCommit := state === s_idle && !blockCommit

location.function_name: RobImp branch-taken trace feedback (dynamic itype update)

findings.finding: The only dynamic trace update in the ROB writeback path is the branch-taken correction: NonTaken (4) → Taken (5) when a conditional branch resolves as taken. There is NO analogous post-commit update for data-side completion. This is consistent with the one-dimensional architecture — once an instruction retires from the ROB, its trace metadata is final. No stale-context vulnerability because data-retirement tracking is not attempted in the first place.

The iretireCommit decoder translates encoded iretire values (from Rename) into scalar instruction retirement counts per commit slot. There is no data-retire count decoder because the concept does not exist. The truth table maps (instrNum, nonRVCNum) → scalar instruction count, consistent with the instruction-retirement-only model. Verified the encoding matches the Rename-stage encode table.
findings.snippet:
val iretireCommit = Wire(Vec(CommitWidth, UInt(IretireWidthCommited.W)))
iretire := chisel3.util.experimental.decode.decoder(
  raw.traceBlockInPipe.iretire,
  TruthTable(instrSizeTable.zipWithIndex.map{case(table, encode) =>
    (BitPat((encode + 1).U(IretireWidthEncoded.W)), BitPat(table._2.U(IretireWidthCommited.W)))},
    BitPat.N(IretireWidthCommited)))

findings.finding: The Itype enumeration uses 4-bit values (0-15) and correctly matches the E-Trace/Smctr transfer type encoding (referenced in smctr.adoc 'transfer-type-defs' table at lines 574-596). Encodings: None=0, Exception=1, Interrupt=2, ExpIntReturn=3, NonTaken=4, Taken=5, UninferableJump=6, reserved=7, UninferableCall=8, InferableCall=9, UninferableTailCall=10, InferableTailCall=11, CoRoutineSwap=12, FunctionReturn=13, OtherUninferableJump=14, OtherInferableJump=15. There are NO Zcmp-specific itype values, confirming XiangShan does not implement Zcmp trace classification. The itype width is fully saturated (4 bits, all 16 slots used), so adding Zcmp would require extending itype width.
findings.snippet:
object Itype extends NamedUInt(4) {
  def None = 0.U; def Exception = 1.U; def Interrupt = 2.U; def ExpIntReturn = 3.U
  def NonTaken = 4.U; def Taken = 5.U; def UninferableJump = 6.U; def reserved = 7.U
  def UninferableCall = 8.U; def InferableCall = 9.U; def UninferableTailCall = 10.U
  def InferableTailCall = 11.U; def CoRoutineSwap = 12.U; def FunctionReturn = 13.U
  def OtherUninferableJump = 14.U; def OtherInferableJump = 15.U
}

findings.finding: Rename generates itype via Itype.jumpTypeGen() which classifies only branch/jump instructions per the E-Trace transfer type definitions. For vector load/store and other non-branch/non-jump instructions (including Zcmp if decoded), jumpTypeGen returns 0.U (None). There is no Zcmp-specific decode path in Rename — Zcmp cm.push/cm.pop instructions are not explicitly handled. IsXret detection for trap returns (ExpIntReturn=3) correctly checks CSR address bits (11,1).orR. The ilastsize assignment correctly uses Mux(lastIsRVC, HalfWord, Word). For fused instructions, itype/ilastsize correctly forward from the next uop.
findings.snippet:
uops(i).traceBlockInPipe.itype := Mux(
  isXret,
  Itype.ExpIntReturn,
  Itype.jumpTypeGen(inVec(i).fuType, inVec(i).fuOpType, ...)
)

findings.finding: CtrlBlock maps TraceBuffer output to TraceCoreInterface as a pure identity pass-through for iretire, itype, and ilastsize. The only transformations are: (a) iaddr resolution via pcMem lookup using ftqIdx+ftqOffset (lines 296-302); (b) priv determination via Mux(Itype.isTrapOrXret, lastPriv, currentPriv) at lines 305-308. The mstatus, trap.cause, and trap.tval come from the CSR block (io.fromCSR.traceCSR). There is no dretire bypass or data-trace path because none exists. These connections are correct for the current one-dimensional architecture.

TraceBuffer compresses adjacent trace blocks by accumulating iretire counts when consecutive blocks don't need separate PC entries (needPcVec driven by inTypeIsNotNoneVec). Compression only preserves iretire and ftqIdx/ftqOffset from the first block. The circular queue (enqPtr/deqPtr) manages TraceEntry storage. blockCommit backpressure stalls the ROB when the buffer can't accept more entries. There is no separate data-retirement entry type or ordering constraint between iretire and dretire events — because dretire events don't exist. The enqueue/dequeue logic operates on a single event type. Internally consistent with the one-dimensional architecture.
